result.topic_en: Riemann's method for the linear hyperbolic equation $\partial^2 w/\partial p\partial q + \partial w/\partial p + \partial w/\partial q = 0$: Green's identity with the adjoint equation, the boundary conditions defining the Riemann function $v$, and a power-series solution $r=\sum p^n q^n/(n!\,n!)$ of $\partial^2 r/\partial p\partial q - r = 0$.
result.transcription:
[sketch: axes; triangle with vertices $p,q'$ (lower left), $p,q$ (top), $p',q$ (right) — labels partly illegible[?]]
$\int v(w+\frac{\partial w}{\partial p})\partial p + w(v-\frac{\partial v}{\partial q})\partial q = 0$
1) $\frac{\partial^2 v}{\partial p\partial q} - \frac{\partial v}{\partial p} - \frac{\partial v}{\partial q} = 0$
$(p=p')\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial q} - v = 0 \quad \frac{\partial v}{\partial p} - v = 0\ (q=q')$
[sketch: corner]
$v = f(p-p', q-q') \quad f(p,q) = r e^{p+q}$

1) $\frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial p\partial q} + \frac{\partial w}{\partial p} + \frac{\partial w}{\partial q} = 0 \qquad 2)\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial p} = \varphi(s)[?] \quad \frac{\partial w}{\partial q} = \psi(s)[?]$
[sketch: closed curve with axes]
$0 = \iint \left(\frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial p\partial q} + \frac{\partial w}{\partial p} + \frac{\partial w}{\partial q}\right) v\, \partial p\, \partial q$
$= \iint \left(\frac{\partial^2 v}{\partial p\partial q} - \frac{\partial v}{\partial p} - \frac{\partial v}{\partial q}\right) w\, \partial p\, \partial q - \int v(w+\frac{\partial w}{\partial p})\partial p + w(v-\frac{\partial v}{\partial q})\partial q$

$\frac{\partial^2 r}{\partial p\partial q} - r = 0 \quad \begin{matrix} q=0 \\ \frac{\partial r}{\partial p} = 0 \\ r=1\end{matrix} \quad \begin{matrix} p=0 \\ \frac{\partial r}{\partial q} = 0 \\ r=1\end{matrix} \qquad q=0\ p=0\ r=1$
[-2-] $r = 1 + \left(\frac{\partial r}{\partial q}\right)_0 q + \dots + \left(\frac{\partial^n r}{\partial q^n}\right)_{q=0} \frac{q^n}{n!}$ \qquad $r = \sum \frac{p^n q^n}{n!\, n!}$
$\frac{\partial^{n+2} r}{\partial p\, \partial q^{n+1}} = \frac{\partial^n r}{\partial q^n}$
$\left(\frac{\partial r}{\partial q}\right)_0 = p + \mathrm{Const.}$ \qquad $\frac{p^n}{n!}$
$\frac{\partial^{n+1} r}{\partial q^{n+1}} = \int_0^p \frac{\partial^n r}{\partial q^n}$
